# Aerun: The Merchant Houses

*A comprehensive guide to the seven great merchant houses that control the Ring Road, the Spice trade, and the coastal city-states of the desert continent.*

## The Noble Alliance and the Ring Road

The outer edge of Aerun is a habitable coastal ring dominated by seven great city-states. While Jak (the Administrator) maintains a presence through the Aura Network and his small temples in these cities, the true power on the continent lies with the noble merchant houses. These families control the **Ring Road**—a massive highway circling the continent—and the global monopoly on **Spice**, a psionic-enhancing byproduct of the Deep Desert's ecosystem.

Recognizing Jak's growing authoritarian control, the seven merchant houses operate in a delicate balance. They tolerate his temples and teleportation monopoly, but use their control over bulk shipping and Spice as leverage. Though united in their desire to maintain independence from the Administrator, the houses are fiercely competitive with one another, engaging in endless games of espionage, price wars, and outright conflict.

Below are the seven major merchant houses that rule the Ring Road.

---

### House Wavir (Balic)

![House Wavir Banner](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/xl7GS8BEdN5onlQjBNVRV4/sandbox/y9MKPea8kIFRmZWOqvolqi-images_1785789517764_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3Byb2plY3RzL2RuZC1sb3N0LXNoaXAtNTNjNmU1ODIvYmFubmVyX3dhdmly.png?__&Key-Pair-Id=K2QY5QTL8JSY6C&Signature=MEQCIFMfjUuukFGxPwn2CWwKcZPjTFHxMddwtwC-hmFtFPyXAiB2J3xozAviGRmHfpX14UL8~C6ws70NXpqrnn0VzoFTwA__)

**Banner:** A silver jozhal on a blue field

House Wavir is one of the most powerful and respected merchant houses on the Ring Road. From their palatial headquarters in Balic, they dominate the shipment of grain, ceramics, and precious metals. Founded centuries ago by a former gladiator named Traxidos Wavir, the house has never forgotten its humble origins.

Wavir is unique among the great houses for its deep and abiding hatred of slavery. They rely entirely on paid labor, employing well-compensated mercenaries, psionicists, and agents. This ideological stance has earned them the loyalty of the common people but the suspicion of rival houses, who often accuse Wavir of secretly funding rebellions. Wavir's business practices are aggressive but strictly adhere to the Merchants' Code. Their massive wealth and heavily fortified outposts make them a dominant force in Ring Road politics, serving as a primary counterweight to more ruthless houses like Tsalaxa.

---

### House Tsalaxa (Draj)

![House Tsalaxa Banner](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/xl7GS8BEdN5onlQjBNVRV4/sandbox/y9MKPea8kIFRmZWOqvolqi-images_1785789517764_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3Byb2plY3RzL2RuZC1sb3N0LXNoaXAtNTNjNmU1ODIvYmFubmVyX3RzYWxheGE.png?__&Key-Pair-Id=K2QY5QTL8JSY6C&Signature=MEUCIDdSk2w32KceTU6PGRqSYaizfJyYhNeFFiwpOQjOHRieAiEAjI5HQ9k6HMr8cU-3Y4FL2w-MbZXtWUljz4jvKdZ6l-I_)

**Banner:** A pair of glaring, bestial yellow eyes on a black field

Infamous throughout Aerun, House Tsalaxa rules the city-state of Draj through espionage, intimidation, and ruthless business practices. While they officially adhere to the Merchants' Code, Tsalaxa is widely known as a den of intriguers whose spies and assassins are second to none.

Tsalaxa specializes in securing valuable trading contracts through blackmail and sabotage. They maintain a vast network of underground tunnels in Draj and heavily fortified supply points along the Ring Road. Their patriarch, Ydris, surrounds himself with a loyal bodyguard of half-giants and employs defilers and cutthroats without hesitation. *"Never cross the dragon or House Tsalaxa"* is a common proverb among Ring Road merchants. They are locked in a bitter, ongoing shadow war with House Wavir.

---

### House Inika (Gulg)

![House Inika Banner](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/xl7GS8BEdN5onlQjBNVRV4/sandbox/y9MKPea8kIFRmZWOqvolqi-images_1785789517764_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3Byb2plY3RzL2RuZC1sb3N0LXNoaXAtNTNjNmU1ODIvYmFubmVyX2luaWth.png?__&Key-Pair-Id=K2QY5QTL8JSY6C&Signature=MEYCIQD-tCwwj4ujpZqsvAZlhkj7gy0ncEAfJkOl48ITImSxTAIhAJSiQXi-VGzqt6WFvdoSyPSEqLbY9lh6hPPYPrUOslXt)

**Banner:** A plain gold circle on a black field

Operating out of the tranquil city of Gulg, House Inika is small by choice but disproportionately wealthy. They specialize in small, high-value cargoes such as kola nuts, exotic feathers, gemstones, and rare spices. Because their caravans are small, fast, and guarded by elite elven scouts, Inika can afford to maintain dozens of active trade routes simultaneously.

Inika's philosophy revolves around efficiency and non-confrontation. When challenged by a rival, Inika rarely meets force with force. Instead, they withdraw, change tactics, and apply devastating economic pressure in unexpected areas — often manipulating the prices of their monopolized goods to ruin competitors. Led by the shrewd matriarch Andiama Inika, the house is famous for its fanatical internal loyalty. They treat their agents incredibly well, ensuring that betrayal from within is almost unheard of.

---

### House Shom (Nibenay)

![House Shom Banner](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/xl7GS8BEdN5onlQjBNVRV4/sandbox/y9MKPea8kIFRmZWOqvolqi-images_1785789517764_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3Byb2plY3RzL2RuZC1sb3N0LXNoaXAtNTNjNmU1ODIvYmFubmVyX3Nob20.png?&Key-Pair-Id=K2QY5QTL8JSY6C&Signature=MEYCIQCkdYXOwRdnSnnMnaOCrBeyd45PwnEj8nEmTPjV387VNAIhALYhqXRqgohQcTa9NQ6IzkB~a5PFtGMIt1I91Srjtmn3)

**Banner:** Three white dragonflies on a red-and-black diagonally divided field

House Shom is an ancient, immensely wealthy, but deeply corrupt house based in the decadent city of Nibenay. Centuries ago, Shom rose to power through brilliant leadership and unusual alliances with desert tribes and thri-kreen warriors. Today, however, the family has succumbed to sybaritic luxury.

The rulers of House Shom rarely leave their silken palaces, preferring to observe the world from curtained palanquins while leaving the actual management of the house to their agents. Predictably, this has led to rampant embezzlement and institutional rot. Shom caravans are massive, slow, and inefficient, and their outposts are wasteful monuments to past glory. Despite this decline, Shom's sheer volume of hoarded wealth and historical momentum keeps them seated at the table of the great houses. A quiet reform movement within the younger ranks of the family struggles to save the house before it collapses under its own weight.

---

### House M'ke (Raam)

![House M'ke Banner](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/xl7GS8BEdN5onlQjBNVRV4/sandbox/y9MKPea8kIFRmZWOqvolqi-images_1785789517764_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3Byb2plY3RzL2RuZC1sb3N0LXNoaXAtNTNjNmU1ODIvYmFubmVyX21rZQ.png?_&Key-Pair-Id=K2QY5QTL8JSY6C&Signature=MEUCIQC-NUCnRISRkZ9okOTn9lLQd7094hucbMQaIeXZTDip5QIgGJI4LAbLfy-1JcuuxT~XGRFYWmXvZLty7ddGjx6y0ns_)

**Banner:** A silver quill pen on a red field

House M'ke is a house of bizarre contradictions, ruling the increasingly unstable city-state of Raam. They are known for being exceptionally courteous and pleasant in person, yet utterly ruthless in business. They treat powerful rivals with intense respect while aggressively preying upon weaker houses, stealing trade routes and engaging in open combat when they sense vulnerability.

Currently, M'ke is in a defensive posture. As the political situation in Raam deteriorates into near-anarchy, M'ke has withdrawn from many of its extended Ring Road routes to fortify its citadels. The house's greatest asset is its legendary hidden wealth — vast caches of coin and resources hoarded during prosperous years and hidden in secret vaults across Aerun. They are using this wealth to hire mercenary armies, attempting to wait out the chaos in Raam while remaining neutral in the growing rebellions.

### House Vordon (Tyr)

![House Vordon Banner](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/xl7GS8BEdN5onlQjBNVRV4/sandbox/y9MKPea8kIFRmZWOqvolqi-images_1785789517764_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3Byb2plY3RzL2RuZC1sb3N0LXNoaXAtNTNjNmU1ODIvYmFubmVyX3ZvcmRvbg.png?&Key-Pair-Id=K2QY5QTL8JSY6C&Signature=MEQCIGXBbGDMWhR4l5zQZZEvD0vs~EijwR5PnAux57SjA9kZAiBWF96iGWMixG-Zd4C0PqYtUGnZx5scYYgPKJRoa8NaoQ__)

**Banner:** A black diamond on a red-brown field

House Vordon is a house of iron and conspiracy. Originally a dominant force that controlled the iron trade across the Ring Road, Vordon suffered a humiliating decline due to the erratic and destructive demands of Tyr's previous rulers. Bankrupted by forced contributions to massive public works, Vordon became a laughingstock among the other houses.

However, Vordon is pragmatic and ambitious. Under the leadership of Patriarch Thaxos, the house is secretly rebuilding its empire. They are using dummy corporations and shadow companies to move goods and hire troops, slowly amassing a secret army. Thaxos intends not only to restore Vordon's monopoly on the iron trade but to eventually seize political control of Tyr itself. Vordon caravans are once again becoming a common sight on the Ring Road, heavily guarded and moving massive shipments of ore and obsidian.

---

### House Stel (Urik)

![House Stel Banner](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/xl7GS8BEdN5onlQjBNVRV4/sandbox/y9MKPea8kIFRmZWOqvolqi-images_1785789517764_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3Byb2plY3RzL2RuZC1sb3N0LXNoaXAtNTNjNmU1ODIvYmFubmVyX3N0ZWw.png?&Key-Pair-Id=K2QY5QTL8JSY6C&Signature=MEUCIQDSBMJGsbDy7YisZ~GsEpiTsvltgKDNCugUYIUqL~qvMQIgNzCV-ejuvEz5SNQhiCvteyOwuyedThzerxx7SGP74TA_)

**Banner:** A pair of crossed black scimitars on a white field

House Stel is the most aggressive and militaristic of the seven great houses. Founded by mercenaries and gladiators, Stel operates out of the warrior-culture city of Urik. Their business model is built around the spoils of war: weapons, slaves, stolen cargo, and mercenary contracts.

Stel's caravans are essentially moving fortresses. While they lack the subtle business acumen of Inika or the vast wealth of Wavir, they suffer fewer losses to raiders than any other house. Stel frequently hires out its elite guards and heavily armored wagons to other houses — including Tsalaxa, with whom they share a close, pragmatic alliance. The house is strictly organized along military lines, and its leaders view Ring Road commerce less as a market and more as a battlefield to be conquered.
